claim: On 2024-11-21 Amazon EC2 added future-dated Capacity Reservations: you can request a Capacity Reservation for a future date instead of only for immediate use.
question: When did Amazon EC2 start to accept Capacity Reservations for a future date?

values.spoken: November twenty-first, twenty twenty-four

values.display: request Capacity Reservations for a future date

evidence.quote: | [Future-dated Capacity Reservations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-capacity-reservations.html) | You can now request Capacity Reservations for a future date. | November 21, 2024 |

note: d032. Older material says a Capacity Reservation starts immediately only.

claim: For a future-dated Capacity Reservation you choose the start date and a commitment duration; billing starts at that date, and during the commitment you can't lower the instance count or the commitment duration below the initial commitment. After the commitment elapses you can modify it in any way or cancel it without charge.
question: What can and can't you change on a future-dated Capacity Reservation during its commitment duration?

values.display: you can't decrease the instance count
values.spoken: during the commitment you can't lower the count or the duration

values.display: cancel it without charge
values.spoken: after the commitment you can change or cancel it for free

evidence.quote: If you request a **future-dated Capacity Reservation**, you specify when you need the capacity and how long you commit to keeping it. At the specified future date, the Capacity Reservation becomes available for use and billing starts. During the commitment duration, you can't decrease the instance count or commitment duration below your initial commitment.
After the commitment duration elapses, you can modify the Capacity Reservation in any way or cancel it without charge.

claim: Cancelling a Capacity Reservation that is active with no commitment duration, or whose commitment duration has elapsed, is free; instances that were running in it keep running at On-Demand rates or at a matching Savings Plans or Regional Reserved Instance rate.
question: What happens to cost and running instances when you cancel a Capacity Reservation without a commitment?

values.display: cancellation is free
values.spoken: cancelling a reservation without a commitment is free

values.display: the instances continue to run normally
values.spoken: running instances keep running

qualifiers.condition: active with no commitment duration or an elapsed commitment duration

evidence.quote: If the Capacity Reservation is `active` with no commitment duration or an elapsed commitment duration, cancellation is free.

If you cancel a Capacity Reservation that has running instances, the instances continue to run normally outside of the Capacity Reservation at standard On-Demand Instance rates or at a discounted rate if you have a matching Savings Plans or Regional Reserved Instance.

claim: On 2026-09-28 AWS announced that you can postpone the start date of a future-dated Capacity Reservation before delivery; the commitment duration can increase, depending on when you postpone.
question: What did the September 2026 change add to future-dated Capacity Reservations?

values.spoken: September twenty-eighth, twenty twenty-six

values.display: you can now postpone your start date

evidence.quote: If your plans change before delivery, you can now postpone your start date to match your new timeline.
The commitment duration can increase, depending on when you postpone the start date.
Before the capacity is delivered, you can postpone the start date. Additional commitment might be required.

note: d032. Announced after 2026-07-15: not examinable yet. The What's New date is 2026-09-28; no document-history row seen.

claim: On 2025-11-21 Amazon EC2 added interruptible Capacity Reservations, which make unused reserved capacity temporarily available for other workloads within your account.
question: When were interruptible Capacity Reservations added, and what are they for?

values.spoken: November twenty-first, twenty twenty-five

values.display: make unused capacity temporarily available

evidence.quote: | [Interruptible Capacity Reservations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/interruptible-capacity-reservations.html) | Interruptible Capacity Reservations help you make unused capacity temporarily available for other workloads within your account. | November 21, 2025 |

note: d037. The What's New post is dated 2025-11-24.

claim: With an interruptible Capacity Reservation the owner can reclaim the capacity at any time; when it is reclaimed, the consumer instances running in it are terminated, with no fallback to On-Demand or Spot, and the capacity returns to the source reservation.
question: What happens to instances in an interruptible Capacity Reservation when the owner reclaims the capacity?

values.display: any running consumer instances are terminated
values.spoken: the consumer instances are terminated

values.display: there is no fallback to On-Demand or Spot
values.spoken: there is no fallback to On-Demand or Spot

evidence.quote: We retain the association between the source reservation and the interruptible Capacity Reservation. As a result, when you reclaim your capacity, any running consumer instances are terminated, and the capacity is restored to your original source reservation.
Your instances will be terminated when the owner reclaims capacity - there is no fallback to On-Demand or Spot.

claim: Interruptible Capacity Reservations are targeted by default, so an instance launch must target them; they can be shared with other accounts or an AWS organization through AWS RAM, and AWS recommends them only for applications that can be interrupted.
question: How do instances use an interruptible Capacity Reservation, and which workloads suit it?

values.display: by default targeted Capacity Reservations
values.spoken: they are targeted, so the launch must target them

values.display: applications that can be interrupted
values.spoken: only for workloads that can be interrupted

evidence.quote: Interruptible Capacity Reservations are by default targeted Capacity Reservations, so you need to target them in your instance launch.
We recommend that you only use interruptible Capacity Reservations for applications that can be interrupted.
After creating an interruptible reservation, you can share it with additional AWS accounts or your AWS organization using AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM).

claim: An interruptible Capacity Reservation is billed as an independent new reservation: the source reservation is billed for total capacity minus the allocated capacity, and the interruptible reservation for the allocated capacity.
question: How is an interruptible Capacity Reservation billed?

values.display: billed for it as an independent new reservation
values.spoken: billing is split between the source and the interruptible reservation

evidence.quote: When you create an interruptible reservation, you're billed for it as an independent new reservation. This splits your billing:
Source reservation: You're billed for total capacity minus allocated capacity
